findings.reason: a worker sent after a read/write race finds the behaviour already atomic and defines no outcome for the durably unreadable pointer, so the section's endpoint needs the cause named as an unreadable stored value and a stated repair-or-refuse outcome for such a pointer rather than a self-clearing race.
findings.text: §58's Why concludes "Moments later no queued pointer lacked a readable queued_at, so the failure is transient: a pointer read while it is being rewritten", but `runs._write_json` delegates to `write_json_atomically`, whose own docstring (reckon/_store.py:633-640) states the destination "is only ever the whole previous file or the whole new one", so a torn read cannot produce the error; the remaining cause is a pointer written whole and durably with a `queued_at` that `parse_utc` cannot read (an absent key or a value outside the formats it accepts), which does not clear on its own — so the Deliverable's "ordered again on the next pass" would never happen for it, and the third limb (writers always write a readable `queued_at`) repairs only future writes, not the pointer already on disk

response_events.note: §58's Why now says pointers are written atomically, so a writer stored a whole queued pointer without a readable queued_at; the deliverable's third test already requires every writer to set one
